utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you. You've had an opportunity to review this report. Could you tell us, does the information accurately reflect the information that was coming from the field in the UNPAs as of the date of this report?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Yes. Sadly, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we look under paragraph 2, first of all, the report states that UNPROFOR assumed responsibility in Sector East on 15 May 1992, in Sector West on 20 June, 1992, and in Sectors North and South on 2 July, 1992. First of all, was that the order of events?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And what is meant by UNPROFOR assumed responsibility? A responsibility for what?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Responsibility essentially for providing security within the UNPA for the -- for the local population, ensuring that demilitarisation. The -- the term there really refers to the fact that UNPROFOR had enough troops available by that time in each of those UNPAs to start carrying out the function. It didn't necessarily mean that the parties had co-operated and honoured their part of the agreement. It simply meant that UNPROFOR had all the resources it was going to get for the job in those UNPAs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: From an internal security perspective, you've already mentioned the problems that were happening with regard to the non-Serb population in the UNPAs. Which of the four sectors was considered the most difficult?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Sector East.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And were you able to come to any conclusions why Sector East? What was going on there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: No. The -- the root cause of Sector East and indeed all the other sectors, Your Honour, was that the parties there, the political parties, never ensured the demilitarisation of those sectors. And by centrally conceived and orchestrated plan sought to circumvent in any ways possible the implementation of a secure environment for the population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And you've told us that Sector East was -- was the worst. How would you rank the other sectors?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Second worst would be south, then north, and finally west.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 and look at paragraph 4 it mention as a major achievement the withdrawal of the JNA from all sectors except for one infantry battalion in Sector East. Could you tell us, how far from the UNPA borders did the JNA withdraw to?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: In Sector East, they withdrew across the Danube river and deployed along the Danube river ready to come back again if they felt the need to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did that cause any problems?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Well, it was highly threatening for the non-Serb population within Sector East, and was also a very prominent threat to the Croatian army that they had better behave or the JNA would come back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: During the JNA withdrawal, what happened to the JNA weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: The JNA took them, all of their weapons and equipment with them, as far as I am aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And what about the equipment of other local Serb forces, the Territorial Defence, and other forces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Well, the -- the Vance Plan provided for heavy weapons belonging to local militias were to be put into a double-lock system and that the -- the weapons of these militias were either to be entrusted to the UN or handed over to the JNA. The reality is that some of the heavy weapons were put into double lock, and just about all of the small arms and lights weapons were retained either openly by -- reuniformed militias had put on police uniforms. All these weapons were hidden in various part of the UNPAs. Effectively the militias didn't disappear. The militias didn't disarm. They were simply camouflaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we look at paragraph 5, it says: "Prior to UNPROFOR's assumption of responsibility in the UNPAs, it had become apparent that the JNA was transferring many of its heavy weapons to local Territorial Defence units and paramilitary militias established in these areas." Were you aware of that problem?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Broadly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: What was going on there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: The JNA were making sure that the military forces that they left behind were capable of defending the UNPA areas with an adequate allocation of heavy weapons if they would be required, if the Croatian forces attempted to recapture them, or they could at least delay the Croat forces long enough for the JNA to come back and recapture the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did the Vance Plan envision that this conversion of JNA resources to local armed forces would happen? Was this envisaged?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. And I believe this is a deliberate circumvention of the intent on the detail of the Vance Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I'd like to turn away briefly from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could have on a the screen 65 ter 1339. This is tab 56.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: This is an UNPROFOR daily sitrep dated 3 November 1992. And if we could look towards the bottom, we see listed CMO. What does that mean for purposes of this report?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: It's -- it's my title as Chief Military Observer. It means that I am to be a recipient of this report. It was a standard distribution list.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 2 and look under Sector East, item 1. And it says: "At Erdut bridge, 3 AA guns, two APC, and one tank reported hidden behind a house." First of all, what does "AA" stand for?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And were these weapons violations of the double-lock system?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Without looking at a map, it could be possible that those -- the numbers given there are a map square. It's possible that they are located on the eastern side of the Danube so it could be legitimate in the sense that -- the JNA. But if we had a map here and I presume that those grid squares are within the UNPA then almost certainly violations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tendered this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2795, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Did UNPROFOR receive any reports on heavy weapon violations from the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the question. Are we talking about the use of them or the presence of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Presence of them.

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Yes. From time to time we would receive correspondence from Croatian authorities alleging that there were weapon storage areas in one location or another or the presence of military elements in various parts of the UNPA.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could look at 65 ter 5273. This is tab 165.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: This is an UNPROFOR memorandum dated 11 October 1992. And if we could turn to page 2. What we have is a letter to UNPROFOR CLO. What is a CLO?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Chief liaison officer, I'm guessing. I just can't see the context there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: It's just because I see on the right-hand side Colonel Petrounev, CLO.

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So there would be an UNPROFOR liaison officer in Zagreb near the Croatian Ministry of Defence, and regular communication between the Croat forces or Croatian forces and UNPROFOR would be through this office.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we can scroll down a little bit. We'll just look at the first page, but they are reporting information regarding a number of hidden weapons at various locations. I see B-1 cannons, ten tanks, some APCs. Could you tell us, was information in reports provided by the Croatian government, were they able to be verified?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: If correspondence was like this was received then it certainly would be investigated. And if it was there, it would be, of course, verified and the issue raised with the local authorities. Sometimes these correspondence like this were based upon imagination. In other cases, there was good, solid intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, may this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2796, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You've -- may have touched upon this in your previous answers. After the JNA formally left the UNPAs, I think you mentioned that there were other armed forces that were there and operating. Could you tell us which ones? What were these forces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Well, and this, Your Honour, is very central, sort of the whole thing, because the militias, some 16.000 of them as a guesstimate, were changed from military army personnel to police forces virtually overnight. There was a process where they changed their uniforms and changed their names but not the function. They still continued to operate. They were called either special police, border police, customs police, it didn't matter. Their role and their reality was to sort of hide the fact that there had been no demilitarisation of the militias within the UNPAs. It was a policy and a programme executed at the highest level with the co-operation, I suspect, of certainly the JNA and the highest political authorities within the Serb political structure. So we ended up with instead of a force of a few thousand or in -- in the case of the Krajina, 7.000 policemen as we know them in a normal civil community, we ended up with some 22.000 policemen in the UNPAs. And this was not -- this was in detail and an intent way of avoiding implementation of the demilitarisation and the agreement in the Vance Plan. The net result was a highly threatening environment for the whole civilian population, particularly non-Serbs. The reality is that much of the ethnic cleansing, much of the violence was carried out by the special policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And how well armed were these special policemen?

utterances.speaker: JOHN BRIAN WILSON
utterances.text: Well, they certainly had side-arms, that is automatic rifles, but they had access to heavy weapons which were hidden throughout the UNPAs also.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours perhaps that is a good time to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Olmsted. Brigadier Wilson, this is it for today. You're not released as a witness. We expect you back tomorrow at 9.00 and not being released as a witness means that you cannot discuss your testimony with anybody in the meantime, and you cannot talk to any of the parties. Thank you very much. The Court Usher will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of August, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
